question: What loss on ignition did the extracted kerogen have, and what does the national standard require?
expect: 88%; the standard requires an LOI greater than 75% (sec. 2.3.3)
rendered:
Table 2.3.3. Kerogen Extraction
The oil shale powder was sequentially treated with 20% hydrochloric acid and a mixed acid (20% hydrochloric acid and 40% hydrofluoric acid mixed at a volume ratio of 1:2) under a 70 °C water bath condition, alternating stirring multiple times to remove inorganic minerals such as carbonates and silicates. The acid-washed samples were washed with deionized water to near neutrality and then placed in a 105 °C oven to dry to a constant weight. 
Upon testing, the loss on ignition (LOI) of the kerogen prepared in this experiment was 88%, satisfying the regulatory requirement of an LOI greater than 75% specified in the national standard.
